jobs.occupation: Student assistant in Customer Care & Business Operation
jobs.description:
At MODU, we design modular building toys developed with a focus on active play and great design. Right now, we are looking for a structured and service-minded part-time colleague or student assistant to help us support our customers during busy peak periods and ensure smooth B2B order logistics — acting as the vital link between our Customer Care, Sales, and Logistics teams.

Your main responsibilities:

• 
Assist our Customer Care team during busy peak periods by answering inquiries from customers across Europe via email and chat

• 
Process, coordinate, and track B2B orders to ensure timely and accurate deliveries to our retail partners

• 
Act as the daily bridge between Customer Care, Sales, and our external warehouse/logistics partners

• 
Proactively follow up on shipments, resolve delivery issues, and handle claims or missing items

• 
Keep order systems and customer data updated and organized

We imagine that you:

• 
Are naturally structured, detail-oriented, and great at keeping a cool head during busy periods

• 
Love solving problems and take pride in following tasks all the way to the finish line

• 
Can work independently and stay connected with the team, whether you are at the office or working from home

• 
Communicate effortlessly and professionally in English (written and spoken)—additional European languages like Danish, German, or French are a big plus

• 
Experience with Shopify and CRM systems are a plus

• 
Are looking for a flexible part-time job alongside your studies or other commitments (experience from customer support or coordination is a plus, but not a requirement)

Practical details:

• 
Employment type: 10-15 hours pr. week / Student position (hourly paid), with flexible hours and extra shifts during peak seasons

• 
Location: Hybrid — a mix of our office in Nørrebro, Copenhagen, and remote work (much of the work can be done remotely)

• 
Application deadline: November 15, 2026

• 
Start date: As soon as possible / Upon agreement

Sounds like the right job for you? We look forward to hearing from you. Send your short application and CV as soon as possible, as we conduct interviews on an ongoing basis.

We encourage all candidates, regardless of gender, age, and background, to apply, and we welcome applications where personal information is kept anonymous or omitted.

Read more about us at www.modutoy.com.

For more information or questions please contact us at clara@modu.dk

**Use your skills to revolutionize HR with Team Spirit and Innovation at NTT DATA

**Are you ready to be a part of a team that is reshaping the world of HR, making a real impact for our clients? As our new Employee Central consultant, you will get to combine leadership, technical expertise and business understanding with your genuine mentor mentality.

**A Close-Knit team – and a One-Stop-Shop for Pioneering HR Solutions

**We would like to invite you into a collaborative and inclusive environment where each member is a vital part of our success. Our culture is laid-back yet professional, with room for a good laugh and a shared commitment to excellence. This can be felt all the way to our clients, who often talk about the enjoyable and effective partnerships they have with us.

“We’re proud of being a comprehensive solution for all things HR – from SuccessFactors and support to strategic HR advisory. And as part of the larger NTT DATA Business Solutions network, we can leverage cutting-edge AI technology, ensuring our clients receive the most advanced and efficient solutions available,” says Danny Haschke, SuccessFactors Consultant.

**Innovative Employee Central Implementation with ready2run®

**As a Senior Employee Central Consultant, you will lead large, international and complex implementations, taking ownership of the Employee Central workstream from design through deployment. ready2run® builds on our preconfigured starting solution, proven delivery framework and the way we shape implementation projects and customer offerings.

**Specifically, You Will

**

• Translate business needs into robust, scalable solutions.

• Help customers benefit from our ready2run® approach – both as a methodology and a mindset.

• Play an important part in strengthening our collective capability by sharing knowledge, supporting collaboration across projects and helping junior consultants grow their confidence and expertise.

**Combine your strong technical expertise with your business understanding

**In this role, you will need a proactive focus on quality, detail and delivery, using your critical thinking skills and experience in resolving complex technical and functional issues in a timely and effective manner. Also, you possess a genuine desire to guide, challenge and develop colleagues, review work and share practical knowledge – and you can do so constructively in international teams. Moreover, with your strong communication skills, you engage effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders and build trusted relationships with colleagues and clients alike.

Finally, we know nobody is perfect, but we imagine that you may:

• Have several years of hands-on experience configuring and implementing SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central.

• Have proven experience leading large, international and complex implementations, with ownership of the Employee Central workstream from design to deployment.

• Possess strong Employee Central solution knowledge, combined with the ability to analyze HR processes and translate business priorities into practical, scalable design.

• Be open to travelling and working on diverse projects, adapting to new challenges and environments.

• Be fluent in English (this is required), with additional Scandinavian languages being a plus.

• The role can be based in any Nordic country, with the expectation that you are within practical daily commuting distance of one of our local offices.

**Will you give us the opportunity to let you shine?

**Applicants are assessed continuously, so do not wait! Apply now and take the first step towards a fulfilling career with us at NTT DATA Business Solutions. We are excited to welcome you and see what we can achieve together.

**Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

**At NTT DATA Business Solutions, we believe our strength lies in our diversity. We proudly embrace people from all walks of life, regardless of ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, religion, or background. Our diverse perspectives fuel innovation and create a richer, more creative work environment for everyone.

_At NTT DATA Business Solutions, we drive innovation – from advisory and implementation to managed services and beyond, powered by a global team of over 19,000 experts representing over 90 nations in more than 30 countries. With SAP at our core and a powerful ecosystem of partners like Microsoft and ServiceNow, we continuously improve solutions and AI-driven technology to make them work for companies – and for their people.

_We are part of NTT DATA, a $30+ _billion business and technology services, AI and digital infrastructure leader. As a Global Top Employer, NTT DATA serves 75% of the Fortune Global 100 and, with experts in over 70 countries, co-innovates solutions that encourage experimentation and recognize great work.

__With us, you have endless opportunities to think big, act bold and take ownership. Make this the place where you belong, learn, and build your network.

_NTT DATA Business Solutions: Make this the place where Y__ou grow.

Do you thrive in the digital landscape and have a strong commercial mindset? As E-tail Coordinator, you’ll play a vital role in growing our E-tail business across the EMEA. You’ll work together with the sales team with top-tier e-tailers to drive brand awareness, visibility, conversion, and sales of Audo´s iconic design products

Your Role and Focus Areas

Together with the local sales teams, you will support and enable our e-tailer sales performance across markets. Your role is to coordinate, align and strengthen e-tail partnerships and activities across borders and provide the local sales teams with the data, insights and support to succeed.

In this role, you will:

• Secure and exceed sales targets through structured online sales initiatives

• Manage and develop relationships with key e-tailers in EMEA together with the local sales team

• Identify new digital opportunities and align with our broader company retail strategy

• Promote the Audo brand through marketing activations and ensure full visibility of product portfolio and commercial campaign planning

• Support partners with insights, Master Data and digital activation

• Drive commercial campaigns and analyzing data

How You’ll Make an Impact

Your success will be measured by how you succeed executing the company´s strategy of our e-tail channel together with the local sales teams.

Key success indicators include:

• Implementation and execution of the e-tail strategy together with the local sales teams

• Growth in e-tail revenue and new product sales

• Drive brand awareness through strategic marketing initiatives

• Strong performance in digital campaigns (Traffic, Call-To-Action, Conversion)

• Customer meetings and brand engagement

Working Smarter with Data

You’ll use data as a compass—tracking performance, identifying trends, and turning insights into action. Your ability to communicate data with the sales teams is key to success.

Your tools and tasks will include:

• Monitoring and interpreting key sales metrics (Average Order Value, Customer Acquisition Cost, conversion rates)

• Creating clear visualizations and performance reports for internal use

• Continuously optimizing efforts based on results and customer feedback

• Data sharing through partner portals

Your Profile

We’re looking for a strong coordinator with digital sales professionals with an eye for online growth.

To succeed in this role, you bring:

• Minimum 3-5 years of experience in e-tail sales

• Experience working with design/lifestyle e-tailers

• Strong knowledge of digital marketing tools and portals

• Excellent communication and relationship-building skills

• Fluency in English

What Drives You

Your mindset is just as important as your skillset. We’re seeking someone who’s hands-on, data-driven, and eager to push boundaries in the e-tail business.

We believe you are:

• Self-motivated and proactive, with a natural drive for results

• Structured and analytical, with strong planning capabilities

• Customer-oriented with a passion for building value-adding partnerships

• A collaborative team player who thrives in a fast-paced environment

Why join us?

• An exciting opportunity to join an ambitious company

• Become part of a diverse, collaborative, and dynamic sales team, reporting directly to the Sales Director – Wholesale & E-tail, European Core Markets

• Competitive salary package, aligned with experience and qualifications

• You will work from our unique Head Office in Nordhavn

• Flexible and collaborative working culture

Excited to develop e-tail business for a brand where design meets purpose?

We’d love to hear from you - please don’t hesitate to apply by submitting your CV and Cover Letter, describing why you are the right fit for this position and why you are interested in joining us.

We encourage you to submit your application as soon as possible.

Are you ready to take the next step in your M&A career and gain hands-on experience across the full deal lifecycle in an international company with ambitious growth plans?

We are looking for an M&A Associate, Corporate Development, to join KK Group and support the execution of our M&A strategy and broader strategic growth agenda. This is an opportunity to work across the full M&A process, from identifying and evaluating potential acquisition opportunities to transaction execution and post-acquisition integration.

You will work closely with key stakeholders across the organization, combining financial analysis with strategic and commercial insights to support important investment decisions.

The role offers early responsibility, broad exposure to M&A and close interaction with senior management within an international group backed by A.P. Møller Holding, where M&A is an important lever for future growth.

The position is based in Copenhagen and requires presence in our Copenhagen office three days per week.

Your role

As an M&A Associate in Corporate Development, your primary responsibility will be to support the development and execution of KK's M&A strategy.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Conduct financial analysis, financial modelling and company valuations to support M&A and other strategic investment decisions.

• Support the execution of M&A transactions, including due diligence, coordination of external advisors, transaction documentation and other deal-related activities.

• Screen and assess potential acquisition targets, including strategic fit, financial performance, valuation and key investment considerations.

• Prepare investment cases, including strategic rationale, financial returns, risks and value creation opportunities.

• Conduct market and competitor analysis to identify potential acquisition targets and assess new markets and growth opportunities.

• Work closely with business divisions and relevant functions to assess commercial, financial and operational aspects of potential acquisitions.

• Support post-acquisition integration planning, including identification and assessment of potential synergies.

• Support broader corporate development and strategic initiatives across the Group.

Your profile

We expect you to have 2-4 years of relevant professional experience, preferably from investment banking, corporate M&A, private equity or Big 4 transaction services. Candidates with a background in strategy consulting and strong financial capabilities will also be considered.

In addition, we expect that you have:

• Strong financial and analytical skills, including experience with financial modelling, valuation and financial statement analysis.

• Experience with M&A transactions, financial due diligence or other transaction-related activities.

• A good commercial understanding and the ability to combine financial analysis with strategic considerations.

• Strong proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint, including the ability to develop clear and well-structured decision material.

• A structured and detail-oriented approach, with the ability to deliver high-quality work within tight deadlines.

• The ability to work independently, take ownership of tasks and challenge assumptions when relevant.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate financial and strategic conclusions clearly.

• A collaborative mindset and the ability to work effectively with stakeholders across functions, countries and organizational levels.

• Fluency in written and spoken English.

We value intellectual curiosity, sound judgement and a willingness to take responsibility. You should be comfortable working in an environment where priorities can change, and where you are expected to take initiative, challenge assumptions and contribute actively.

Ready to build your M&A experience, take responsibility early on and contribute to KK Group’s next phase of growth? We would love to hear from you.

jobs.occupation: Senior Contract and Warranty Manager – Hobro, Denmark
jobs.description:
Do you have experience in managing complex operations contracts and commercial risk across countries? Do you enjoy building something into the next level?

We are looking for a Senior Contract and Warranty Manager to take end-to-end ownership of operations contracts across Eurowind Energy's global wind, solar and BESS portfolio.

Who we are

Eurowind Energy is a global and leading developer, owner and operator of energy parks. Based in Denmark, we operate in 16 countries around Europe and in the USA, and we are continuously growing our project portfolio. We believe in a future of renewable energy, and we have an ambitious plan of becoming the next generation's "Power Major". Based on a full value chain from greenfield project development to energy trading, more than 700 team members are dedicated to creating a greener future fueled with nothing but renewable energy!

We are looking for an experienced Senior Contract and Warranty Manager to join our Global Operations team. Based at our Operations office in Hobro, you will be the contract and warranty specialist for our global asset portfolio, supporting colleagues and managers across countries and functions.

Your role

As Senior Contract and Warranty Manager, you will take ownership of key commercial agreements, claims and warranty matters across Eurowind Energy's global asset portfolio. You will work closely with Asset Management, Operations, Finance, Legal and local teams to ensure that our contractual rights are understood, protected and actively used. The role combines hands-on contract management with a strong focus on risk, value creation and standardization across markets.

• Own contract management for operations contracts, including service and O&M agreements, warranty and performance guarantees, grid connection and curtailment compensation, insurance, land lease and supplier agreements

• Lead negotiation, drafting and execution of contracts so they meet both legal and commercial requirements

• Identify, assess and mitigate commercial and legal risk across the contract portfolio

• Manage claims and warranty follow-up, making sure issues are tracked, escalated and resolved in line with contractual terms

• Build global contract templates, playbooks and governance processes that work consistently across countries

• Monitor contract performance and compliance, flagging risks and improvement opportunities

• Be the go-to contact for the country teams and the wider operations organisation on contract questions and disputes

You will work with the country operations teams, Strategic Commercial Management (which owns PPAs, power trading and balancing contracts), Technical Operations, Investor Administration, SCADA Operations, Legal, Finance, and suppliers and service providers. Your role is to strengthen the countries' ability to manage contracts locally, not to add another layer of bureaucracy.

What we offer

You will join Global Operations at a time where we are transforming how we manage and operate our global asset portfolio. You will get a broad international scope, close collaboration across functions and countries, and the opportunity to work with complex commercial and operational challenges. We offer a high level of autonomy, a strong professional environment and the opportunity to make a visible impact on how Eurowind operates.

• A newly created role where you set the structures and ways of working

• The chance to make a real impact on how we improve and operate our commercial mindset

• Ownership, trust and room to shape your own area

• A global role with some travel, in an international and energetic environment

• A workplace in Hobro, alongside our operations colleagues

You will join a newly established team and report to Louise Guldager Thomsen, Head of Global Commercial Management. Louise is a collaborative and pragmatic leader who builds strong relationships, creates alignment across functions and empowers people to take ownership. She combines a deep understanding of the organisation with a practical focus on execution and a global perspective.

Required competencies and skills

You have solid experience with contract management, commercial agreements, warranties and/or claims, ideally from the energy, infrastructure, construction or other asset-intensive industries. You are comfortable navigating complex contractual matters and working across technical, commercial and legal topics. You combine strong analytical and negotiation skills with a pragmatic approach and the ability to turn contractual knowledge into action and business value.

• Significant experience in contract management within energy, infrastructure, renewables or another asset-intensive industry

• A proven record of leading complex contract negotiations end-to-end, including service and O&M, warranty, grid/curtailment, insurance and supplier contracts

• Solid understanding of commercial and legal risk management, with experience building or applying compliance frameworks

• Relevant legal, commercial or technical education (for example law, business or engineering), or equivalent hands-on experience

• International experience and comfort working across countries and cultures

• Enjoys building something new and setting up structures from scratch

• Works autonomously across a global organisation and values being part of a team

• Structured and detail-oriented, yet pragmatic about getting things done without unnecessary process

• Communicates clearly and directly, holding suppliers and internal stakeholders accountable while working with respect

Please note that this role requires a clean criminal record.

Renewable energy is our future. And so are our people!

At Eurowind Energy we do our best to create a culture where everyone is valued and feels at home. You will notice this in your everyday work life, where you have the freedom to speak up and where your voice means something to us. We know that when you grow, we grow. Therefore, we strive to support you in what you believe is right and in your personal and professional development. We offer you an exciting job in an energetic and international environment. And we promise you: the wind is never standing still.

Developing, operating and managing wind and solar parks is not just pure business for us. It is a way to view the world. And with this worldview comes a genuine ambition to be one of the leading developers in Europe. Because creating a future run entirely on green energy matters to us.

We manage our own portfolio of projects and at the same time, we perform technical and financial management of projects. We have throughout many years experienced sustained economic growth in the number of developed projects and companies in management. And we continue to expect this. Simply because it is in our nature to keep developing – projects, companies and our people.

Read more about Eurowind Energy A/S on our website or LinkedIn

Did we capture your attention?

Great! If you see yourself in this role, do not hesitate to apply for the position. Please use the link below. As we continuously review incoming applications, please send us your CV as soon as possible.

Should you have any questions before applying, please feel free to contact Louise Guldager Thomsen, Head of Global Commercial Management, at lth@ewe.dk.

Application deadline: 30 November 2026

Place of work: Hobro, Denmark

Do you want to help protect critical energy infrastructure at the heart of the green transition? Are you energised by working directly with local businesses across Europe, understanding their challenges and mobilising the right expertise to solve them?

Who we are

Eurowind Energy is a global and leading developer, owner and operator of energy parks. Based in Denmark, we operate in 16 countries around Europe and in the USA, and we are continuously growing our project portfolio. We believe in a future of renewable energy, and we have an ambitious plan of becoming the next generation's "Power Major". Based on a full value chain from greenfield project development to energy trading, more than 700 team members are dedicated to creating a greener future fueled with nothing but renewable energy!

We are looking for an experienced Global Cyber Security Consultant to join our team in Hobro, Denmark.

As an operator of critical energy infrastructure, cybersecurity is a vital part of how we protect our business, our partners and the communities we serve. As Eurowind continues to grow and adapt to an evolving threat landscape and regulatory requirements such as NIS2, we are strengthening security as an integrated part of the organisation – in every market where we operate.

You will join our Group Cyber and Information Security team – a small, senior team supporting a global organisation, anchored directly with the CISO. Cyber and information security is delivered centrally from Group headquarters to all our markets, and we do not scale through headcount alone, but through expertise, smart automation and AI. That means real ownership, meaningful responsibility and the opportunity to shape how security is delivered across Eurowind.

Your role

This is a new and highly visible role. As Group Cyber Security Advisor, you are Group Cyber and Information Security’s face in our 14 markets. You build trusted relationships with country management and site teams – remotely and, when it adds value, on site – and uncover where they need help within cyber and information security – from regulatory compliance and supplier risk to securing operational technology at our energy parks.

You will not solve everything yourself, and you are not expected to. Behind you stands the full Group organisation: security operations, architecture, GRC and legal specialists who deliver the concrete solutions. Your job is to identify the need, activate the right expertise at headquarters, and support the local organisation through implementation – so our markets get consistent, high-quality security support from within the Group instead of relying on external consultants.

Your work will include:

• Acting as the primary point of contact for cyber and information security in our local markets and building strong relationships with country management

• Conducting structured assessments of local needs, risks and maturity – across IT, OT and compliance – using a common Group framework

• Translating local needs into concrete deliveries from Group specialists in security operations, GRC, legal and architecture

• Supporting local implementation of Group security initiatives, standards and controls, including NIS2, ISO 27001 and IEC 62443 requirements

• Making our markets aware of the security services already available to them through the Group, reducing the need for external advisors

• Reporting findings, progress and risks back to the CISO and contributing to Group-level prioritisation

What we offer

We believe security starts with understanding the business: what needs protecting, why it matters and how security can help the organisation move faster and more safely. That is exactly what this role embodies – security delivered in partnership with the business, not imposed on it.

Our role is not to block progress, but to help Eurowind operate securely and confidently globally, under NIS2 and in an increasingly demanding threat landscape.

We also believe good security starts with strong fundamentals. It is easy to chase the cutting edge, but most organisations are exposed because the basics are not consistently in place. For us, that means strong visibility, reliable detection and well-practised response – consistently, in every market. We do not dismiss bold ideas – we build the foundation that makes them viable.

Just as importantly, we believe better security comes from building a better team. We value people who challenge assumptions, think independently and bring different perspectives. Leadership in our team is about creating the conditions for better answers to emerge, not pretending to have all the answers.

In return, you will get:

• A unique, self-directed role with international reach and direct impact across 14 countries

• Direct anchoring with the CISO and close collaboration with senior stakeholders across the Group

• A strong specialist backline – you are the front figure, never alone with the problem

• Access to modern AI tools and automation to amplify your impact

• Pension and health insurance

• Flexible working hours and a hybrid working model based at our headquarters in Hobro – with the opportunity to travel to our European markets when it makes a difference

Required competencies and skills

This role is less about deep technical specialisation and more about judgement, communication and drive. You are comfortable walking into a country office or an energy park and earning trust quickly – whether you are talking to a country manager, a site technician or a local lawyer. You can hold a conversation about regulatory obligations in the morning and OT security at a substation in the afternoon, and you know when to bring in a specialist.

We imagine you bring:

• Solid experience within cyber and information security, for example from consulting, advisory or a broad security role in an international organisation

• A working understanding of regulatory frameworks such as NIS2, and ideally exposure to OT/industrial environments or IEC 62443

• Strong stakeholder management skills and the credibility to engage with local management

• A structured and analytical way of working – you turn conversations into clear assessments and actionable requests

• The confidence to work independently across borders while knowing when to pull in the backline

• Excellent communication skills in English; additional European languages are an advantage

• Willingness to travel occasionally across our 14 markets

It’s a plus if you have:

• Experience from the energy sector or other critical infrastructure

• Experience working in a Group/HQ function delivering services to local entities

• Hands-on experience with security assessments, gap analyses or audit-style engagements

• Used AI or LLMs as practical tools in your workflow

Please note that this role requires a clean criminal record. A security clearance may become relevant later in the employment, but it is not required in order to apply.

At Eurowind Energy we do our best to create a culture where everyone is valued and feels at home. You will notice this in your everyday work life, where you have the freedom to speak up and where your voice means something to us. We know that when you grow, we grow. Therefore, we strive to support you in what you believe is right and in your personal and professional development. We offer you an exciting job in an energetic and international environment. And we promise you: the wind is never standing still.

Developing, operating and managing wind and solar parks is not just pure business for us. It is a way to view the world. And with this worldview comes a genuine ambition to be one of the leading developers in Europe. Because creating a future run entirely on green energy matters to us.

We manage our own portfolio of projects and at the same time, we perform technical and financial management of projects. We have throughout many years experienced sustained economic growth in the number of developed projects and companies in management. And we continue to expect this. Simply because it is in our nature to keep developing – projects, companies and our people.

Great! If you see yourself in this role, do not hesitate to apply for the position. Please use the link below. As we continuously review incoming applications, please send us your CV as soon as possible.

Do you want to make sure that when something goes wrong, our organisation already knows what to do? Are you energised by building capability and confidence in others, rather than being the one who has to solve every incident yourself?

Who we are

Eurowind Energy is a global and leading developer, owner and operator of energy parks. Based in Denmark, we operate in 16 countries around Europe and in the USA, and we are continuously growing our project portfolio. We believe in a future of renewable energy, and we have an ambitious plan of becoming the next generation's "Power Major". Based on a full value chain from greenfield project development to energy trading, more than 700 team members are dedicated to creating a greener future fueled with nothing but renewable energy!

We are looking for an experienced Global Resilience Consultant to join our team in Hobro, Denmark.

As an operator of critical energy infrastructure, our ability to respond when things go wrong is fundamental to protecting our business, our partners and the communities we serve. As Eurowind continues to grow and face an evolving risk landscape and regulatory requirements such as NIS2, we are strengthening emergency preparedness as an integrated part of the organisation – in every market where we operate.

You will join our Group Cyber and Information Security team – a small, senior team supporting a global organisation, anchored directly with the CISO. Emergency preparedness is coordinated centrally from Group headquarters across all our markets, and we do not scale through headcount alone, but through clear plans, practised people and smart use of technology. That means real ownership, meaningful responsibility and the opportunity to shape how prepared Eurowind is when it matters most.

Your role

This is a new and highly visible role. As Group Emergency Preparedness Advisor, you own that Eurowind is ready before a crisis happens – not that you personally run the response when one occurs. You make sure our global emergency preparedness has the plans it needs, that those plans are kept current and fit for purpose across all markets, and that the people who will use them are trained and confident enough to act.

You will not run our incident response or crisis management yourself, and you are not expected to. That responsibility stays with the teams and leaders whose job it is to respond when something happens. Your job is to build and maintain the framework behind them – the plans, the training and the exercises – so that when a crisis hits, everyone already knows their role.

Your work will include:

• Owning Eurowind’s global emergency preparedness framework – making sure the crisis management, business continuity and incident response plans we need actually exist, across all markets

• Mapping which plans are in place, where, and identifying and closing gaps together with local management and Group functionsin

• Driving larger, cross-market crisis exercises as well as frequent smaller micro-exercises – so readiness is tested and kept sharp continuously, not just checked off once a year

• Making sure plans and training cover the full range of scenarios relevant to Eurowind – from cyber incidents to safety events, operational disruptions and OT/critical infrastructure incidents

• Working with country management, Group functions such as security, legal, communications and HR, and site teams to keep plans realistic and grounded in how the organisation actually operates

• Reporting on preparedness status, training coverage and identified gaps back to the CISO and contributing to Group-level prioritisation

What we offer

We believe preparedness only counts if it works under pressure. A plan nobody has practised is not a plan – it is a document. That is exactly what this role is about: making sure Eurowind is drilled, not just documented.

We are moving towards an approach that is more structured, tested and better integrated across the business. Our role is not to own every response, but to make sure Eurowind can respond – confidently and consistently – globally, under NIS2 and in an increasingly demanding risk landscape.

We also believe good preparedness starts with strong fundamentals. It is easy to write an impressive plan, but most organisations are exposed because the basics are not consistently trained and practised. For us, that means clear ownership, tested plans and people who know what to do – consistently, in every market. We do not dismiss ambition – we build the foundation that makes it viable.

Just as importantly, we believe better preparedness comes from building a better team. We value people who challenge assumptions, think independently and bring different perspectives. Leadership in our team is about creating the conditions for better answers to emerge, not pretending to have all the answers.

In return, you will get:

• A unique, self-directed role with international reach and direct impact across 14 countries

• Direct anchoring with the CISO and close collaboration with senior stakeholders across the Group

• A clear mandate to build capability rather than carry the operational burden alone – you own the framework, not every incident

• Access to modern AI tools and automation to amplify your impact

• Pension and health insurance

• Flexible working hours and a hybrid working model based at our headquarters in Hobro – with the opportunity to travel to our European markets when it makes a difference

Required competencies and skills

This role is less about being the person in the room during a crisis, and more about the discipline and drive to make sure everyone else knows what to do when they are. You are comfortable walking into a country office or an energy park and earning trust quickly – whether you are talking to a country manager, a site technician or a Group specialist. You know how to turn “we should probably have a plan for that” into a plan people have actually practised.

We imagine you bring:

• Solid experience within crisis management, business continuity or emergency preparedness, for example from consulting, advisory or a broad security or resilience role in an international organisation

• A structured and analytical way of working – you can map the current state, spot the gaps and turn them into concrete plans and training

• Experience designing and delivering exercises at different scales – from full crisis simulations to quick, recurring micro-exercises

• Strong stakeholder management skills and the credibility to engage with local management across cultures

• A working understanding of regulatory frameworks relevant to preparedness, such as NIS2

• Excellent communication skills in English; additional European languages are an advantage

• Willingness to travel occasionally across our 14 markets

It’s a plus if you have:

• Experience from the energy sector or other critical infrastructure

• Experience working in a Group/HQ function delivering services to local entities

• Familiarity with standards such as ISO 22301 (business continuity) or IEC 62443 (OT security)

• Used AI or LLMs as practical tools in your workflow

Please note that this role requires a clean criminal record. A security clearance may become relevant later in the employment, but it is not required in order to apply.

At Eurowind Energy we do our best to create a culture where everyone is valued and feels at home. Therefore, we strive to support you in what you believe is right and in your personal and professional development. We offer you an exciting job in an energetic and international environment. jobs.occupation: New paradigm to disentangle hydrothermal stresses and assess regional agricultural vulnerability to drought-heatwave events
jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Agroecology programme. The position is available from 15 March 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title
New paradigm to disentangle hydrothermal stresses and assess regional agricultural vulnerability to drought-heatwave events

Research area and project description
The Department of Agroecology at Aarhus University, Denmark, invites applications for a three-year PhD position in remote sensing and knowledge-guided machine learning to assess agricultural vulnerability to drought and heatwaves. The expected starting date is 15 March 2027. The position is supported by the Sino-Danish Center for Education and Research (SDC) and involves collaboration with Chinese Academy of Sciences, including a research stay of 12 months.

Food security, climate change and biodiversity loss represent three major environmental sustainability challenges. The Center for Landscape Research in Sustainable Agricultural Futures (Land-CRAFT), established in June 2022, with expertise in biogeochemistry, agronomy and climate-impact research. This PhD project aims to develop a knowledge-guided machine-learning framework that combines remote sensing, field observations and process-based models to disentangle interacting stresses and assess agricultural vulnerability at regional scales. The research will distinguish the effects of soil water limitation, vapour pressure deficit, and temperature on crop productivity. The resulting knowledge and methods will support early warning, precision irrigation and agricultural climate-risk assessment.

The PhD student will work on three interconnected research tasks:
1. Develop an integrated observation framework for crop drought and heat responses. Combine thermal infrared, multispectral and hyperspectral remote sensing with soil moisture measurements, meteorological observations and field data to characterise crop responses across contrasting environmental conditions.
2. Disentangle the individual and interacting effects of water and heat stress. Quantify how soil-water availability, atmospheric demand and temperature influence crop functioning and productivity, and identify the conditions under which their interactions intensify crop stress.
3. Assess regional agricultural vulnerability to compound drought–heatwave events.
Scale the identified stress-response relationships from field observations to regional assessments, identifying vulnerability patterns, critical thresholds and hotspots.

SDC is a partnership between all eight Danish universities and the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences (UCAS). It brings together Danish and Chinese research and education environments through collaborative research, joint supervision and international mobility. Participation offers the PhD student opportunities to gain research experience in both countries and build an international scientific network.

More about SDC

The student will be employed at Aarhus University, with Sheng Wang as the main supervisor with Kiril Manevski, Suxia Liu and Yongqiang Zhang as co-supervisors. During the research stay in Beijing, the student will collaborate with the hydrology and land-surface modelling group at the Institute of Geographic Sciences and Natural Resources Research, CAS. The student will contribute to SDC’s MSc educational activities. The SDC framework offers the option of pursuing a double PhD degree from Aarhus University and UCAS, subject to an institutional agreement and fulfilment of both universities’ requirements. SDC PhD framework.

For further information, please reach out swan@agro.au.dk.

Qualifications and specific competences
We are searching for a highly motivated candidate who has an M.Sc. degree in geoinformatics, remote sensing, agriculture, environmental sciences, data sciences, geography, ecology, or closely related fields.

Demonstrated oral and written communication skills in English are required. The applicant must be able to present results at international conferences and publish in international peer-reviewed journals. The applicant should be enthusiastic about working in an international and interdisciplinary academic environment. Applications from women and people from underrepresented groups are strongly encouraged. Further, we will prefer candidates with some of the following qualifications:

 * Advanced Programming & Big Data: Strong programming skills (preferably in Python) and experience handling large-scale, multi-source remote sensing datasets and cloud-computing platforms.
 * Rich experience in satellite remote sensing for crop yield prediction and stress analysis. Good scientific and technical writing skills.
 * Strong skills in programming (preferably in Python), large-scale remote sensing data processing, radiative transfer modelling and deep learning. Direct experience or strong background in deep learning or knowledge-guided machine learning.
 * An ability to communicate effectively in English, and will contribute to dissemination, teaching and reporting research outcome in high-impact scientific journals.
 * An ability and interest to collaborate across disciplinary.
 * Collaborative and interpersonal skills and will contribute positively to the social working environment.

Place of employment and place of work

jobs.description:
PhD in Physical AI for Adaptive Robot Manipulation
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Electrical and Computer Engineering programme. The position is available from 01 March 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title
PhD in Physical AI for Adaptive Robot Manipulation

Research area and project description
Applications are invited for a fully funded three-year PhD position at the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Aarhus University. The position is part of STORM (Soft Tactile Memory for Safe Physical-AI Correction of Robotic Foundation Models), a new project funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark (DFF). The candidate will join the Adaptive & Agentic AI (A3) Lab, headed by Dr. Behzad Bozorgtabar (main supervisor), and will work closely with Professor Ahmad Rafsanjani and the SDU Soft Robotics group, who are developing the soft tactile skin.

Research vision
How can a robot foundation model use physical feedback to correct an action during execution? Models such as vision-language-action (VLA) and world-action models let robots follow natural-language instructions, but they act on what they see rather than on what they feel. When a grasp begins to slip or a fragile object deforms, the camera view often looks fine until the damage is done. STORM gives robotic foundation models a sense of touch, so that a robot can notice when a manipulation is going wrong and correct itself safely while it acts.

PhD project
The candidate will develop the machine-learning core of STORM. The work spans three connected scientific questions, leaving room for the candidate to shape the specific algorithmic directions: (1) How can contact representations be learned from advanced tactile interfaces, including a soft-fluidic tactile skin developed at SDU? (2) How can predictive models forecast how contact states should evolve over short horizons under a policy's intended actions? (3) How can the mismatch between expected and felt contact drive parameter-efficient adaptation of pre-trained foundation policies while guaranteeing safety? Methods will be evaluated on public benchmark and real-world robotic setup, focusing on dexterous manipulation of fragile and unseen objects as well as safe human-robot interaction.

Environment
The project sits at the intersection of machine learning, Physical AI, robot foundation models (e.g., VLA and World-Action models), world models, tactile sensing, and adaptation algorithms—areas in which the A3 Lab publishes regularly at top-tier venues such as NeurIPS, ICLR, CVPR, and CoRL. The PhD includes a possible planned research stay at KTH Royal Institute of Technology in Stockholm, and close collaboration with the SDU team.

Qualifications and specific competences
This is a highly selective position; applicants are expected to meet the requirements below.

Education: A master’s degree (120 ECTS or equivalent) in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, Electrical/Computer Engineering, or a related quantitative field, completed or nearing completion before the start date.

Technical Skills: Advanced proficiency in Python and PyTorch, with hands-on experience training, fine-tuning, or adapting modern deep architecture such as Transformers, state-space/sequence models, and diffusion or flow-matching models.

Core Knowledge: A strong foundation in machine learning, deep learning, or computer vision, combined with a strong motivation to work on Physical AI, multimodal tactile sensing, world models, and online adaptation, etc.

Relevant Research Experience (one or more of the following is highly advantageous):
 
• Robot & Policy Learning: Imitation learning, behavior cloning, offline/model-based RL, or policy learning for manipulation (e.g., diffusion policies, Vision-Language-Action models, or World-Action models), as well as familiarity with manipulation benchmarks (e.g., LIBERO, CALVIN, or ManiSkill).
• World Models & Sequential Representation Learning: Self-supervised learning on temporal or multimodal sensor streams, action-conditioned video/dynamics prediction, latent world models, or uncertainty estimation.
• Model Adaptation & Post-Training: Test-time adaptation (TTA), continual/online learning, parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT/LoRA), or safe/constrained policy updates.
Hands-on Robotics: Prior experience with physical robot platforms, grippers, tactile/force sensors, and ROS 2 is an advantage, but not strictly required for candidates with an exceptional machine learning background. However, a strong willingness to work with physical hardware and run real-robot experiments is required.

Track Record: Evidence of strong research potential—such as a strong master’s thesis, open-source research code, or publications/submissions at leading ML, vision, or robotics venues (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, CoRL, RSS, ICRA)—is a strong advantage.

Attributes: A mindset for scientific rigor, reproducibility, and open-source contribution, the ability to collaborate across algorithmic AI and physical hardware teams, and excellent written and spoken English.

Application Requirements (How to Apply)
Please ensure your application includes the following documents:
• Statement of Interest (1 page): Detailing your background in machine learning, computer vision or robotics, any work experience relevant to the position, and your motivation for joining the A3 Lab and the project.
• Curriculum Vitae: Including a publication list (if applicable) and a technical project page, with links to code repositories or videos of experiments where available.
• Academic Records: Transcripts and diplomas (Bachelor’s and Master’s).Project Description Requirement: The candidate is required to use the project description from the PhD announcement.

Place of employment and place of work
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Adaptive & Agentic AI (A3) Lab, Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE), Faculty of Technical

Contacts
Applicants seeking further information regarding the PhD position are invited to contact:
 
• Behzad Bozorgtabar, e-mail: behzad@ece.au.dk (main supervisor)
For information about application requirements and mandatory attachments, please see our application guide. If answers cannot be found there, please contact:
• admission.gradschool.tech@au.dk 
How to apply:
Please follow this link to submit your application.

Application deadline is 04 January 2027 at 23:59 CET

Preferred starting date is 01 March 2027

For technical reasons, you must upload a project description. Please copy the project description above and upload it as a PDF in the application.

Please note:
• Only documents received prior to the application deadline will be evaluated. Thus, documents sent after deadline will not be considered.
• The programme committee may request further information or invite the applicant to attend an interview.
• Shortlisting will be used, which means that the evaluation committee only will evaluate the most relevant applications.
Formalities and salary range
Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions. You will be employed as an academic staff member at basic salary grades 4–8. As a PhD fellow you will also receive a monthly non-pensionable allowance.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

The application must be submitted via the online recruitment system, which can be accessed under ‘How to apply’.
